texts.sng.2.16: O meu amado é meu, e eu sou d’elle: elle apascenta o seu rebanho entre os lyrios.
texts.sng.2.17: Até que sopre o dia, e fujam as sombras, volta, amado meu: faze-te similhante á corça ou ao filho dos veados sobre os montes de Bether.
texts.sng.3.1: De noite busquei em minha cama a quem a minha alma ama: busquei-o, e não o achei.
texts.sng.3.2: Levantar-me-hei, pois, e rodearei a cidade; pelas ruas e pelas praças buscarei a quem ama a minha alma: busquei-o; e não o achei.
texts.sng.3.3: Acharam-me os guardas, que rondavam pela cidade: eu lhes perguntei: Vistes a quem ama a minha alma?
texts.sng.3.4: Apartando-me eu um pouco d’elles, logo achei a quem ama a minha alma: agarrei-me a elle, e não o larguei, até que o introduzi em casa de minha mãe, na camara d’aquella que me gerou.
texts.sng.3.5: Conjuro-vos, ó filhas de Jerusalem, pelas corças e cervas do campo, que não acordeis, nem desperteis o meu amor, até que queira.
texts.sng.3.6: Quem é esta que sobe do deserto, como umas columnas de fumo, perfumada de myrrha, de incenso, e de toda a sorte de pós do especieiro?
texts.sng.3.7: Eis que é a cama de Salomão; sessenta valentes estão ao redor d’ella, dos valentes d’Israel:
texts.sng.3.8: Todos armados d’espadas, dextros na guerra: cada um com a sua espada á coxa por causa dos temores nocturnos.
texts.sng.3.9: O rei Salomão fez para si um thalamo de madeira do Libano.
texts.sng.3.10: Fez-lhe as columnas de prata, o estrado d’oiro, o assento de purpura, o interior coberto com o amor das filhas de Jerusalem.
texts.sng.3.11: Sahi, ó filhas de Sião, e contemplae ao rei Salomão com a corôa com que o coroou sua mãe no dia do seu desposorio e no dia do jubilo do seu coração.
texts.sng.4.1: Eis que és formosa, amiga minha, eis que és formosa: os teus olhos são como os das pombas entre as tuas tranças: o teu cabello é como o rebanho de cabras que pastam no monte de Gilead.
texts.sng.4.2: Os teus dentes são como o rebanho das ovelhas tosquiadas, que sobem do lavadouro, e todas ellas produzem gemeos, e nenhuma ha esteril entre ellas.
texts.sng.4.3: Os teus labios são como um fio d’escarlate, e o teu fallar é doce: a fonte da tua cabeça como um pedaço de romã entre as tuas tranças.
texts.sng.4.4: O teu pescoço é como a torre de David, edificada para pendurar armas: mil escudos pendem d’ella, todos rodellas de valorosos.
texts.sng.4.5: Os teus dois peitos são como dois filhos gemeos da corça, que se apascentam entre os lyrios.
texts.sng.4.6: Até que sopre o dia, e fujam as sombras, irei ao monte da myrrha e ao outeiro do incenso.
texts.sng.4.7: Tu és toda formosa, amiga minha, e em ti não ha mancha.
texts.sng.4.8: Vem comigo do Libano, ó esposa, comigo do Libano vem: olha desde o cume de Amana, desde o cume de Senir e de Hermon, desde as moradas dos leões, desde os montes dos leopardos.
texts.sng.4.9: Tiraste-me o coração, irmã minha, ó esposa: tiraste-me o coração com um dos teus olhos, com um collar do teu pescoço.
texts.sng.4.10: Que bellos são os teus amores, irmã minha! oh esposa minha! quanto melhores são os teus amores do que o vinho! e o cheiro dos teus unguentos do que o de todas as especiarias!
texts.sng.4.11: Favos de mel estão manando dos teus labios, ó esposa! mel e leite estão debaixo da tua lingua, e o cheiro dos teus vestidos é como o cheiro do Libano.
texts.sng.4.12: Jardim fechado és tu, irmã minha, esposa minha, manancial fechado, fonte sellada.
texts.sng.4.13: Os teus renovos são um pomar de romãs, com fructos excellentes, o cypreste com o nardo,
texts.sng.4.14: O nardo, e o açafrão, o calamo, e a canella, com toda a sorte d’arvores d’incenso, a myrrha e aloes, com todas as principaes especiarias.
texts.sng.4.15: És a fonte dos jardins, poço das aguas vivas, que correm do Libano!
texts.sng.4.16: Levanta-te, vento norte, e vem tu, vento sul: assopra no meu jardim, para que distillem os seus aromas: ah! se viesse o meu amado para o seu jardim, e comesse os seus fructos excellentes!
texts.sng.5.1: Já vim para o meu jardim, irmã minha, ó esposa: colhi a minha myrrha com a minha especiaria, comi o meu favo com o meu mel, bebi o meu vinho com o meu leite: comei, amigos, bebei, ó amados, e embriagae-vos.
texts.sng.5.2: Eu estava dormindo, mas o meu coração vigiava: eis a voz do meu amado que estava batendo: abre-me, irmã minha, amiga minha, pomba minha, perfeita minha, porque a minha cabeça está cheia d’orvalho, as minhas guedelhas das gottas da noite;
texts.sng.5.3: Já despi os meus vestidos; como os tornarei a vestir? já lavei os meus pés; como os tornarei a sujar?
texts.sng.5.4: O meu amado metteu a sua mão pelo buraco da porta, e as minhas entranhas estremeceram por amor d’elle.
texts.sng.5.5: Eu me levantei para abrir ao meu amado, e as minhas mãos distillavam myrrha, e os meus dedos gottejavam myrrha sobre as aldrabas da fechadura.
texts.sng.5.6: Eu abri ao meu amado, mas já o meu amado se tinha retirado, e tinha ido: a minha alma se derreteu quando elle fallou; busquei-o e não o achei, chamei-o, e não me respondeu.
texts.sng.5.7: Acharam-me os guardas que rondavam pela cidade: espancaram-me, feriram-me, tiraram-me o meu véu os guardas dos muros.
texts.sng.5.8: Conjuro-vos, ó filhas de Jerusalem, que, se achardes o meu amado, lhe digaes que estou enferma de amor.
texts.sng.5.9: Que é o teu amado mais do que outro amado, ó tu, a mais formosa entre as mulheres? que é o teu amado mais do que outro amado, que tanto nos conjuraste?
texts.sng.5.10: O meu amado é candido e rubicundo; elle traz a bandeira entre dez mil.
texts.sng.5.11: A sua cabeça é como o oiro mais apurado, as suas guedelhas crespas, pretas como o corvo.
texts.sng.5.12: Os seus olhos são como os das pombas junto ás correntes das aguas, lavados em leite, postos em engaste.
texts.sng.5.13: As suas faces são como um canteiro de especiaria, como caixas aromaticas; os seus labios são como lyrios que gottejam myrrha distillante.
texts.sng.5.14: As suas mãos como anneis d’oiro que teem engastadas as turquezas: o seu ventre como alvo marfim, coberto de saphiras.
texts.sng.5.15: As suas pernas como columnas de marmore, fundadas sobre bases de oiro puro; o seu parecer como o Libano, excellente como os cedros.
texts.sng.5.16: O seu fallar é muitissimo suave, e todo elle totalmente desejavel. Tal é o meu amado, e tal o meu amigo, ó filhas de Jerusalem.
texts.sng.6.1: Para onde foi o teu amado, ó mais formosa entre as mulheres? para onde virou a vista o teu amado, e o buscaremos comtigo?
texts.sng.6.2: O meu amado desceu ao seu jardim, aos canteiros da especiaria, para se apascentar nos jardins e para colher os lyrios.
texts.sng.6.3: Eu sou do meu amado, e o meu amado é meu: elle se apascenta entre os lyrios.
texts.sng.6.4: Formosa és, amiga minha, como Tirza, aprazivel como Jerusalem, formidavel como um exercito com bandeiras.
texts.sng.6.5: Desvia de mim os teus olhos, porque elles me perturbam. O teu cabello é como o rebanho das cabras que pastam em Gilead.
texts.sng.6.6: Os teus dentes são como o rebanho d’ovelhas que sobem do lavadouro, e todas produzem gemeos, e não ha esteril entre ellas.
texts.sng.6.7: Como um pedaço de romã, assim são as tuas faces entre as tuas tranças.
texts.sng.6.8: Sessenta são as rainhas, e oitenta as concubinas, e as virgens sem numero.
texts.sng.6.9: Porém uma é a minha pomba, a minha perfeita, a unica de sua mãe, e a mais querida de aquella que a pariu: vendo-a, as filhas a chamarão bemaventurada, as rainhas e as concubinas a louvarão.
texts.sng.6.10: Quem é esta que apparece como a alva do dia, formosa como a lua, lustrosa como o sol, formidavel como um exercito com bandeiras?
texts.sng.6.11: Desci ao jardim das nogueiras, para ver os novos fructos do valle, a ver se floresciam as vides e brotavam as romeiras.
texts.sng.6.12: Antes de eu o sentir, me poz a minha alma nos carros do meu povo voluntario.
texts.sng.6.13: Volta, volta, ó Sulamitha, volta, volta, para que nós te vejamos. Porque olhas para a Sulamitha como para as fileiras de dois exercitos?
texts.sng.7.1: Que formosos são os teus pés nos sapatos, ó filha do principe! As voltas de tuas coxas são como joias, segundo a obra de mãos d’artifice.
texts.sng.7.2: O teu umbigo como uma taça redonda, a que não falta bebida; o teu ventre como montão de trigo, sitiado de lyrios.
texts.sng.7.3: Os teus dois peitos como dois filhos gemeos da corça.
texts.sng.7.4: O teu pescoço como a torre de marfim: os teus olhos como os viveiros de Hesbon, junto á porta de Bath-arabbim: o teu nariz como torre do Libano, que olha para Damasco.
texts.sng.7.5: A tua cabeça sobre ti é como o monte Carmelo, e os cabellos da tua cabeça como a purpura: o rei está atado ás varandas.
texts.sng.7.6: Quão formosa, e quão aprazivel és, ó amor em delicias!
texts.sng.7.7: Esta tua estatura é similhante á palmeira; e os teus peitos são similhantes aos cachos d’uvas.
texts.sng.7.8: Dizia eu: Subirei á palmeira, pegarei de seus ramos; e então os teus peitos serão como os cachos na vide, e o cheiro dos teus narizes como os das maçãs.
texts.sng.7.9: E o teu paladar como o bom vinho para o meu amado, que se bebe suavemente, e faz com que fallem os labios dos que dormem.
texts.sng.7.10: Eu sou do meu amado, e elle me tem affeição.
texts.sng.7.11: Vem, ó amado meu, saiamos nós ao campo, passemos as noites nas aldeias.
texts.sng.7.12: Levantemo-nos de manhã para ir ás vinhas, vejamos se florescem as vides, se se abre a flor, se já brotam as romeiras; ali te darei o meu grande amor.
texts.sng.7.13: As mandragoras dão cheiro, e ás nossas portas ha toda a sorte d’excellentes fructos, novos e velhos: ó amado meu, eu os guardei para ti.
texts.sng.8.1: Ah! quem me dera que me fôras como irmão, e mamáras os peitos de minha mãe! que te achara na rua, e te beijára, e nem me desprezariam!
texts.sng.8.2: Te levaria e introduziria na casa de minha mãe, e tu me ensinarias; e te daria a beber vinho aromatico e do mosto das minhas romãs.
texts.sng.8.3: A sua mão esquerda esteja debaixo da minha cabeça, e a sua direita me abrace.
texts.sng.8.4: Conjuro-vos, ó filhas de Jerusalem, que não acordeis nem desperteis o meu amor, até que queira.
texts.sng.8.5: Quem é esta que sobe do deserto, e vem encostada tão aprazivelmente ao seu amado? Debaixo d’uma macieira te despertei, ali te produziu tua mãe com dores; ali te produziu com dores aquella que te pariu.
texts.sng.8.6: Põe-me como sello sobre o teu coração, como sello sobre o teu braço, porque o amor é forte como a morte, e duro como a sepultura o ciume: as suas brazas são brazas de fogo, labaredas do Senhor.
texts.sng.8.7: As muitas aguas não poderiam apagar este amor, nem os rios afogal-o: ainda que desse alguem toda a fazenda de sua casa por este amor, certamente a desprezariam.
texts.sng.8.8: Temos uma irmã pequena, que ainda não tem peitos: que faremos a esta nossa irmã, no dia em que d’ella se fallar?
texts.sng.8.9: Se ella fôr um muro, edificaremos sobre ella um palacio de prata; e, se ella fôr uma porta, a cercaremos com taboas de cedro.
texts.sng.8.10: Eu sou um muro, e os meus peitos são como umas torres: então eu era aos seus olhos como aquella que acha paz.
texts.sng.8.11: Teve Salomão uma vinha em Baal-hamon; entregou esta vinha a uns guardas; e cada um lhe trazia pelo seu fructo mil peças de prata.
texts.sng.8.12: A minha vinha que tenho está diante de mim: as mil peças de prata são para ti, ó Salomão, e duzentas para os guardas do seu fructo.
texts.sng.8.13: Ó tu, a que habitas nos jardins, para a tua voz os companheiros attentam; faze-m’a pois tambem ouvir.
texts.sng.8.14: Vem depressa, amado meu, e faze-te similhante ao corço ou ao filho dos veados sobre os montes dos aromas.

texts.sng.1.1: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.
texts.sng.1.2: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.
texts.sng.1.3: Because of the savor of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.
texts.sng.1.4: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers; we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.
texts.sng.1.5: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
texts.sng.1.6: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but my own vineyard have I not kept.
texts.sng.1.7: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?
texts.sng.1.8: If thou knowest not, O thou fairest among women, go forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds tents.
texts.sng.1.9: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.
texts.sng.1.10: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.
texts.sng.1.11: We will make for thee borders of gold with studs of silver.
texts.sng.1.12: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth its smell.
texts.sng.1.13: A bundle of myrrh is my well beloved to me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
texts.sng.1.14: My beloved is to me as a cluster of camphor in the vineyards of En-gedi.
texts.sng.1.15: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes.
texts.sng.1.16: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yes, pleasant: also our bed is green.
texts.sng.1.17: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
texts.sng.2.1: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
texts.sng.2.2: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
texts.sng.2.3: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
texts.sng.2.4: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
texts.sng.2.5: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick with love.
texts.sng.2.6: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.
texts.sng.2.7: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not, nor awake my love, till he please.
texts.sng.2.8: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
texts.sng.2.9: My beloved is like a roe, or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, showing himself through the lattice.
texts.sng.2.10: My beloved spoke, and said to me, Rise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
texts.sng.2.11: For lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone.
texts.sng.2.12: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
texts.sng.2.13: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
texts.sng.2.14: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
texts.sng.2.15: Take for us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.
texts.sng.2.16: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
texts.sng.2.17: Until the day shall break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
texts.sng.3.1: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
texts.sng.3.2: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
texts.sng.3.3: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
texts.sng.3.4: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
texts.sng.3.5: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
texts.sng.3.6: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
texts.sng.3.7: Behold his bed, which is Solomon's; sixty valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
texts.sng.3.8: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
texts.sng.3.9: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.
texts.sng.3.10: He made its pillars of silver, the bottom of it of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst of it being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
texts.sng.3.11: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown with which his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
texts.sng.4.1: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
texts.sng.4.2: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; all of which bear twins, and none is barren among them.
texts.sng.4.3: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of pomegranate within thy locks.
texts.sng.4.4: Thy neck is like the tower of David built for an armory, on which hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
texts.sng.4.5: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
texts.sng.4.6: Until the day shall break, and the shadows flee away, I will repair to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
texts.sng.4.7: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.
texts.sng.4.8: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
texts.sng.4.9: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thy eyes, with one chain of thy neck.
texts.sng.4.10: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thy ointments than all spices!
texts.sng.4.11: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honey-comb; honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
texts.sng.4.12: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
texts.sng.4.13: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphor, with spikenard,
texts.sng.4.14: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
texts.sng.4.15: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
texts.sng.4.16: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
texts.sng.5.1: I have come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh, with my spice; I have eaten my honey-comb with my honey; I have drank my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yes, drink abundantly, O beloved.
texts.sng.5.2: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
texts.sng.5.3: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
texts.sng.5.4: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
texts.sng.5.5: I rose up to open to my beloved: and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet-smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
texts.sng.5.6: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spoke: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
texts.sng.5.7: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my vail from me.
texts.sng.5.8: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick with love.
texts.sng.5.9: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
texts.sng.5.10: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chief among ten thousand.
texts.sng.5.11: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
texts.sng.5.12: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
texts.sng.5.13: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet-smelling myrrh.
texts.sng.5.14: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
texts.sng.5.15: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
texts.sng.5.16: His mouth is most sweet: yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
texts.sng.6.1: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.
texts.sng.6.2: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
texts.sng.6.3: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
texts.sng.6.4: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
texts.sng.6.5: Turn away thy eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
texts.sng.6.6: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, of which every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.
texts.sng.6.7: As a piece of pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.
texts.sng.6.8: There are sixty queens, and eighty concubines, and virgins without number.
texts.sng.6.9: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yes, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
texts.sng.6.10: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
texts.sng.6.11: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.
texts.sng.6.12: Or ere I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.
texts.sng.6.13: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
texts.sng.7.1: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
texts.sng.7.2: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: thy belly is like a heap of wheat set about with lilies.
texts.sng.7.3: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
texts.sng.7.4: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thy eyes like the fish-pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh towards Damascus.
texts.sng.7.5: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel, and the hair of thy head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.
texts.sng.7.6: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
texts.sng.7.7: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.
texts.sng.7.8: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of its boughs: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;
texts.sng.7.9: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
texts.sng.7.10: I am my beloved's, and his desire is towards me.
texts.sng.7.11: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
texts.sng.7.12: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourisheth, whether the tender grape appeareth, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.
texts.sng.7.13: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
texts.sng.8.1: O that thou wert as my brother, that was nourished at the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yes, I should not be despised.
texts.sng.8.2: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother's house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
texts.sng.8.3: His left hand should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.
texts.sng.8.4: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not, nor awake my love, until he please.
texts.sng.8.5: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple-tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth that bore thee.
texts.sng.8.6: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thy arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals of it are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.
texts.sng.8.7: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
texts.sng.8.8: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
texts.sng.8.9: If she is a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she is a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.
texts.sng.8.10: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favor.
texts.sng.8.11: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out the vineyard to keepers; every one for the fruit of it was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.
texts.sng.8.12: My vineyard which is mine, is before me: thou, O Solomon, must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit of it two hundred.
texts.sng.8.13: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear it.
texts.sng.8.14: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of spices.

texts.sng.1.1: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.
texts.sng.1.2: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; For thy love is better than wine.
texts.sng.1.3: Thine ointments savour sweetly; Thy name is an ointment poured forth: Therefore do the virgins love thee.
texts.sng.1.4: Draw me, we will run after thee! -- The king hath brought me into his chambers -- We will be glad and rejoice in thee, We will remember thy love more than wine. They love thee uprightly.
texts.sng.1.5: I am black, but comely, daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, As the curtains of Solomon.
texts.sng.1.6: Look not upon me, because I am black; Because the sun hath looked upon me. My mother's children were angry with me: They made me keeper of the vineyards; Mine own vineyard have I not kept.
texts.sng.1.7: Tell me, thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest [thy flock], Where thou makest it to rest at noon; For why should I be as one veiled Beside the flocks of thy companions?
texts.sng.1.8: If thou know not, thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds' booths.
texts.sng.1.9: I compare thee, my love, To a steed in Pharaoh's chariots.
texts.sng.1.10: Thy cheeks are comely with bead-rows, Thy neck with ornamental chains.
texts.sng.1.11: We will make thee bead-rows of gold With studs of silver.
texts.sng.1.12: While the king is at his table, My spikenard sendeth forth its fragrance.
texts.sng.1.13: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved unto me; He shall pass the night between my breasts.
texts.sng.1.14: My beloved is unto me a cluster of henna-flowers In the vineyards of Engedi.
texts.sng.1.15: Behold, thou art fair, my love; Behold, thou art fair: thine eyes are doves.
texts.sng.1.16: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant; Also our bed is green.
texts.sng.1.17: The beams of our houses are cedars, Our rafters are cypresses.
texts.sng.2.1: I am a narcissus of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.
texts.sng.2.2: As the lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.
texts.sng.2.3: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons: In his shadow have I rapture and sit down; And his fruit is sweet to my taste.
texts.sng.2.4: He hath brought me to the house of wine, And his banner over me is love.
texts.sng.2.5: Sustain ye me with raisin-cakes, Refresh me with apples; For I am sick of love.
texts.sng.2.6: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.
texts.sng.2.7: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, till he please.
texts.sng.2.8: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he cometh Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.
texts.sng.2.9: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young hart. Behold, he standeth behind our wall, He looketh in through the windows, Glancing through the lattice.
texts.sng.2.10: My beloved spake and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
texts.sng.2.11: For behold, the winter is past, The rain is over, it is gone:
texts.sng.2.12: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of singing is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;
texts.sng.2.13: The fig-tree melloweth her winter figs, And the vines in bloom give forth [their] fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away!
texts.sng.2.14: My dove, in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the precipice, Let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
texts.sng.2.15: Take us the foxes, The little foxes, that spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in bloom.
texts.sng.2.16: My beloved is mine, and I am his; He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies,
texts.sng.2.17: Until the day dawn, and the shadows flee away. Turn, my beloved: be thou like a gazelle or a young hart, Upon the mountains of Bether.
texts.sng.3.1: On my bed, in the nights, I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
texts.sng.3.2: I will rise now, and go about the city; In the streets and in the broadways Will I seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
texts.sng.3.3: The watchmen that go about the city found me: -- Have ye seen him whom my soul loveth?
texts.sng.3.4: -- Scarcely had I passed from them, When I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, Until I had brought him into my mother's house, And into the chamber of her that conceived me.
texts.sng.3.5: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, till he please.
texts.sng.3.6: Who is this, [she] that cometh up from the wilderness Like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all powders of the merchant? ...
texts.sng.3.7: Behold his couch, Solomon's own: Threescore mighty men are about it, Of the mighty of Israel.
texts.sng.3.8: They all hold the sword, Experts in war; Each hath his sword upon his thigh Because of alarm in the nights.
texts.sng.3.9: King Solomon made himself a palanquin Of the wood of Lebanon.
texts.sng.3.10: Its pillars he made of silver, Its support of gold, Its seat of purple; The midst thereof was paved [with] love By the daughters of Jerusalem.
texts.sng.3.11: Go forth, daughters of Zion, And behold king Solomon With the crown wherewith his mother crowned him In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the gladness of his heart.
texts.sng.4.1: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thine eyes are doves behind thy veil; Thy hair is as a flock of goats, On the slopes of mount Gilead.
texts.sng.4.2: Thy teeth are like a flock of shorn sheep, Which go up from the washing; Which have all borne twins, And none is barren among them.
texts.sng.4.3: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, And thy speech is comely; As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples Behind thy veil.
texts.sng.4.4: Thy neck is like the tower of David, Built for an armoury: A thousand bucklers hang thereon, All shields of mighty men.
texts.sng.4.5: Thy two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, Which feed among the lilies.
texts.sng.4.6: Until the day dawn, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, And to the hill of frankincense.
texts.sng.4.7: Thou art all fair, my love; And there is no spot in thee.
texts.sng.4.8: [Come] with me, from Lebanon, [my] spouse, With me from Lebanon, -- Come, look from the top of Amanah, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions' dens, From the mountains of the leopards.
texts.sng.4.9: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, [my] spouse; Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.
texts.sng.4.10: How fair is thy love, my sister, [my] spouse! How much better is thy love than wine! And the fragrance of thine ointments than all spices!
texts.sng.4.11: Thy lips, [my] spouse, drop [as] the honeycomb; Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
texts.sng.4.12: A garden enclosed is my sister, [my] spouse; A spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
texts.sng.4.13: Thy shoots are a paradise of pomegranates, with precious fruits; Henna with spikenard plants;
texts.sng.4.14: Spikenard and saffron; Calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; Myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
texts.sng.4.15: A fountain in the gardens, A well of living waters, Which stream from Lebanon.
texts.sng.4.16: Awake, north wind, and come, [thou] south; Blow upon my garden, [that] the spices thereof may flow forth. Let my beloved come into his garden, And eat its precious fruits.
texts.sng.5.1: I am come into my garden, my sister, [my] spouse; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, beloved ones!
texts.sng.5.2: I slept, but my heart was awake. The voice of my beloved! he knocketh: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, mine undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.
texts.sng.5.3: -- I have put off my tunic, how should I put it on? I have washed my feet, how should I pollute them? --
texts.sng.5.4: My beloved put in his hand by the hole [of the door]; And my bowels yearned for him.
texts.sng.5.5: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the lock.
texts.sng.5.6: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself; he was gone: My soul went forth when he spoke. I sought him, but I found him not; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
texts.sng.5.7: The watchmen that went about the city found me; They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
texts.sng.5.8: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, ... What will ye tell him? -- That I am sick of love.
texts.sng.5.9: What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, Thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, That thou dost so charge us?
texts.sng.5.10: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.
texts.sng.5.11: His head is [as] the finest gold; His locks are flowing, black as the raven;
texts.sng.5.12: His eyes are like doves by the water-brooks, Washed with milk, fitly set;
texts.sng.5.13: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, raised beds of sweet plants; His lips lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
texts.sng.5.14: His hands gold rings, set with the chrysolite; His belly is bright ivory, overlaid [with] sapphires;
texts.sng.5.15: His legs, pillars of marble, set upon bases of fine gold: His bearing as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars;
texts.sng.5.16: His mouth is most sweet: Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, yea, this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
texts.sng.6.1: Whither is thy beloved gone, Thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside? And we will seek him with thee.
texts.sng.6.2: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens and to gather lilies.
texts.sng.6.3: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies.
texts.sng.6.4: Thou art fair, my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as troops with banners:
texts.sng.6.5: Turn away thine eyes from me, For they overcome me. Thy hair is as a flock of goats On the slopes of Gilead.
texts.sng.6.6: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep Which go up from the washing; Which have all borne twins, And none is barren among them.
texts.sng.6.7: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples Behind thy veil.
texts.sng.6.8: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number:
texts.sng.6.9: My dove, mine undefiled, is but one; She is the only one of her mother, She is the choice one of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and they called her blessed; The queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
texts.sng.6.10: Who is she that looketh forth as the dawn, Fair as the moon, clear as the sun, Terrible as troops with banners?
texts.sng.6.11: I went down into the garden of nuts, To see the verdure of the valley, To see whether the vine budded, Whether the pomegranates blossomed.
texts.sng.6.12: Before I was aware, My soul set me upon the chariots of my willing people.
texts.sng.6.13: Return, return, O Shulamite; Return, return, that we may look upon thee. -- What would ye look upon in the Shulamite? -- As it were the dance of two camps.
texts.sng.7.1: How beautiful are thy footsteps in sandals, O prince's daughter! The roundings of thy thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of an artist.
texts.sng.7.2: Thy navel is a round goblet, [which] wanteth not mixed wine; Thy belly a heap of wheat, set about with lilies;
texts.sng.7.3: Thy two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle;
texts.sng.7.4: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; Thine eyes, [like] the pools in Heshbon, By the gate of Bath-rabbim; Thy nose like the tower of Lebanon, Which looketh toward Damascus;
texts.sng.7.5: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel, And the locks of thy head like purple; The king is fettered by [thy] ringlets!
texts.sng.7.6: How fair and how pleasant art thou, [my] love, in delights!
texts.sng.7.7: This thy stature is like to a palm-tree, And thy breasts to grape clusters.
texts.sng.7.8: I said, I will go up to the palm-tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof; And thy breasts shall indeed be like clusters of the vine, And the fragrance of thy nose like apples,
texts.sng.7.9: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine, ... That goeth down smoothly for my beloved, And stealeth over the lips of them that are asleep.
texts.sng.7.10: I am my beloved's, And his desire is toward me.
texts.sng.7.11: -- Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the fields; Let us lodge in the villages.
texts.sng.7.12: We will go up early to the vineyards, We will see if the vine hath budded, [If] the blossom is opening, And the pomegranates are in bloom: There will I give thee my loves.
texts.sng.7.13: The mandrakes yield fragrance; And at our gates are all choice fruits, new and old: I have laid them up for thee, my beloved.
texts.sng.8.1: Oh that thou wert as my brother, That sucked the breasts of my mother! Should I find thee without, I would kiss thee; And they would not despise me.
texts.sng.8.2: I would lead thee, bring thee into my mother's house; Thou wouldest instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate.
texts.sng.8.3: His left hand would be under my head, And his right hand embrace me.
texts.sng.8.4: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, ... Why should ye stir up, why awake [my] love, till he please?
texts.sng.8.5: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? I awoke thee under the apple-tree: There thy mother brought thee forth; There she brought thee forth [that] bore thee.
texts.sng.8.6: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, As a seal upon thine arm: For love is strong as death; Jealousy is cruel as Sheol: The flashes thereof are flashes of fire, Flames of Jah.
texts.sng.8.7: Many waters cannot quench love, Neither do the floods drown it: Even if a man gave all the substance of his house for love, It would utterly be contemned.
texts.sng.8.8: We have a little sister, And she hath no breasts: What shall we do for our sister In the day when she shall be spoken for? --
texts.sng.8.9: If she be a wall, We will build upon her a turret of silver; And if she be a door, We will enclose her with boards of cedar.
texts.sng.8.10: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers; Then was I in his eyes as one that findeth peace.
texts.sng.8.11: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon: He let out the vineyard unto keepers; Every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand silver-pieces.
texts.sng.8.12: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: The thousand [silver-pieces] be to thee, Solomon; And to the keepers of its fruit, two hundred.
texts.sng.8.13: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, The companions hearken to thy voice: Let me hear [it].
texts.sng.8.14: Haste, my beloved, And be thou like a gazelle or a young hart Upon the mountains of spices.

texts.sng.1.1: The Song of Songs, that [is] Solomon's.
texts.sng.1.2: Let him kiss me with kisses of his mouth, For better [are] thy loves than wine.
texts.sng.1.3: For fragrance [are] thy perfumes good. Perfume emptied out -- thy name, Therefore have virgins loved thee!
texts.sng.1.4: Draw me: after thee we run, The king hath brought me into his inner chambers, We do joy and rejoice in thee, We mention thy loves more than wine, Uprightly they have loved thee!
texts.sng.1.5: Dark [am] I, and comely, daughters of Jerusalem, As tents of Kedar, as curtains of Solomon.
texts.sng.1.6: Fear me not, because I [am] very dark, Because the sun hath scorched me, The sons of my mother were angry with me, They made me keeper of the vineyards, My vineyard -- my own -- I have not kept.
texts.sng.1.7: Declare to me, thou whom my soul hath loved, Where thou delightest, Where thou liest down at noon, For why am I as one veiled, By the ranks of thy companions?
texts.sng.1.8: If thou knowest not, O fair among women, Get thee forth by the traces of the flock, And feed thy kids by the shepherds' dwellings!
texts.sng.1.9: To my joyous one in chariots of Pharaoh, I have compared thee, my friend,
texts.sng.1.10: Comely have been thy cheeks with garlands, Thy neck with chains.
texts.sng.1.11: Garlands of gold we do make for thee, With studs of silver!
texts.sng.1.12: While the king [is] in his circle, My spikenard hath given its fragrance.
texts.sng.1.13: A bundle of myrrh [is] my beloved to me, Between my breasts it lodgeth.
texts.sng.1.14: A cluster of cypress [is] my beloved to me, In the vineyards of En-Gedi!
texts.sng.1.15: Lo, thou [art] fair, my friend, Lo, thou [art] fair, thine eyes [are] doves!
texts.sng.1.16: Lo, thou [art] fair, my love, yea, pleasant, Yea, our couch [is] green,
texts.sng.1.17: The beams of our houses [are] cedars, Our rafters [are] firs, I [am] a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys!
texts.sng.2.1: As a lily among the thorns,
texts.sng.2.2: So [is] my friend among the daughters!
texts.sng.2.3: As a citron among trees of the forest, So [is] my beloved among the sons, In his shade I delighted, and sat down, And his fruit [is] sweet to my palate.
texts.sng.2.4: He hath brought me in unto a house of wine, And his banner over me [is] love,
texts.sng.2.5: Sustain me with grape-cakes, Support me with citrons, for I [am] sick with love.
texts.sng.2.6: His left hand [is] under my head, And his right doth embrace me.
texts.sng.2.7: I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes or by the hinds of the field, Stir not up nor wake the love till she please!
texts.sng.2.8: The voice of my beloved! lo, this -- he is coming, Leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
texts.sng.2.9: My beloved [is] like to a roe, Or to a young one of the harts. Lo, this -- he is standing behind our wall, Looking from the windows, Blooming from the lattice.
texts.sng.2.10: My beloved hath answered and said to me, `Rise up, my friend, my fair one, and come away,
texts.sng.2.11: For lo, the winter hath passed by, The rain hath passed away -- it hath gone.
texts.sng.2.12: The flowers have appeared in the earth, The time of the singing hath come, And the voice of the turtle was heard in our land,
texts.sng.2.13: The fig-tree hath ripened her green figs, And the sweet-smelling vines have given forth fragrance, Rise, come, my friend, my fair one, yea, come away.
texts.sng.2.14: My dove, in clefts of the rock, In a secret place of the ascent, Cause me to see thine appearance, Cause me to hear thy voice, For thy voice [is] sweet, and thy appearance comely.
texts.sng.2.15: Seize ye for us foxes, Little foxes -- destroyers of vineyards, Even our sweet-smelling vineyards.
texts.sng.2.16: My beloved [is] mine, and I [am] his, Who is delighting among the lilies,
texts.sng.2.17: Till the day doth break forth, And the shadows have fled away, Turn, be like, my beloved, To a roe, or to a young one of the harts, On the mountains of separation!
texts.sng.3.1: On my couch by night, I sought him whom my soul hath loved; I sought him, and I found him not!
texts.sng.3.2: -- Pray, let me rise, and go round the city, In the streets and in the broad places, I seek him whom my soul hath loved! -- I sought him, and I found him not.
texts.sng.3.3: The watchmen have found me, (Who are going round about the city), `Him whom my soul have loved saw ye?'
texts.sng.3.4: But a little I passed on from them, Till I found him whom my soul hath loved! I seized him, and let him not go, Till I brought him in unto the house of my mother -- And the chamber of her that conceived me.
texts.sng.3.5: I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes or by the hinds of the field, Stir not up nor wake the love till she please!
texts.sng.3.6: Who [is] this coming up from the wilderness, Like palm-trees of smoke, Perfumed [with] myrrh and frankincense, From every powder of the merchant?
texts.sng.3.7: Lo, his couch, that [is] Solomon's, Sixty mighty ones [are] around it, Of the mighty of Israel,
texts.sng.3.8: All of them holding sword, taught of battle, Each his sword by his thigh, for fear at night.
texts.sng.3.9: A palanquin king Solomon made for himself, Of the wood of Lebanon,
texts.sng.3.10: Its pillars he made of silver, Its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, Its midst lined [with] love, By the daughters of Jerusalem.
texts.sng.3.11: Go forth, and look, ye daughters of Zion, On king Solomon, with the crown, With which his mother crowned him, In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the joy of his heart!
texts.sng.4.1: Lo, thou [art] fair, my friend, lo, thou [art] fair, Thine eyes [are] doves behind thy veil, Thy hair as a row of the goats That have shone from mount Gilead,
texts.sng.4.2: Thy teeth as a row of the shorn ones That have come up from the washing, For all of them are forming twins, And a bereaved one is not among them.
texts.sng.4.3: As a thread of scarlet [are] thy lips, And thy speech [is] comely, As the work of the pomegranate [is] thy temple behind thy veil,
texts.sng.4.4: As the tower of David [is] thy neck, built for an armoury, The chief of the shields are hung on it, All shields of the mighty.
texts.sng.4.5: Thy two breasts [are] as two fawns, Twins of a roe, that are feeding among lilies.
texts.sng.4.6: Till the day doth break forth, And the shadows have fled away, I will get me unto the mountain of myrrh, And unto the hill of frankincense.
texts.sng.4.7: Thou [art] all fair, my friend, And a blemish there is not in thee. Come from Lebanon, O spouse,
texts.sng.4.8: Come from Lebanon, come thou in. Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Shenir and Hermon, From the habitations of lions, From the mountains of leopards.
texts.sng.4.9: Thou hast emboldened me, my sister-spouse, Emboldened me with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.
texts.sng.4.10: How wonderful have been thy loves, my sister-spouse, How much better have been thy loves than wine, And the fragrance of thy perfumes than all spices.
texts.sng.4.11: Thy lips drop honey, O spouse, Honey and milk [are] under thy tongue, And the fragrance of thy garments [Is] as the fragrance of Lebanon.
texts.sng.4.12: A garden shut up [is] my sister-spouse, A spring shut up -- a fountain sealed.
texts.sng.4.13: Thy shoots a paradise of pomegranates, With precious fruits,
texts.sng.4.14: Cypresses with nard -- nard and saffron, Cane and cinnamon, With all trees of frankincense, Myrrh and aloes, with all chief spices.
texts.sng.4.15: A fount of gardens, a well of living waters, And flowings from Lebanon!
texts.sng.4.16: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south, Cause my garden to breathe forth, its spices let flow, Let my beloved come to his garden, And eat its pleasant fruits!
texts.sng.5.1: I have come in to my garden, my sister-spouse, I have plucked my myrrh with my spice, I have eaten my comb with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, drink, Yea, drink abundantly, O beloved ones!
texts.sng.5.2: I am sleeping, but my heart waketh: The sound of my beloved knocking! `Open to me, my sister, my friend, My dove, my perfect one, For my head is filled [with] dew, My locks [with] drops of the night.'
texts.sng.5.3: I have put off my coat, how do I put it on? I have washed my feet, how do I defile them?
texts.sng.5.4: My beloved sent his hand from the net-work, And my bowels were moved for him.
texts.sng.5.5: I rose to open to my beloved, And my hands dropped myrrh, Yea, my fingers flowing myrrh, On the handles of the lock.
texts.sng.5.6: I opened to my beloved, But my beloved withdrew -- he passed on, My soul went forth when he spake, I sought him, and found him not. I called him, and he answered me not.
texts.sng.5.7: The watchmen who go round about the city, Found me, smote me, wounded me, Keepers of the walls lifted up my veil from off me.
texts.sng.5.8: I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved -- What do ye tell him? that I [am] sick with love!
texts.sng.5.9: What [is] thy beloved above [any] beloved, O fair among women? What [is] thy beloved above [any] beloved, That thus thou hast adjured us?
texts.sng.5.10: My beloved [is] clear and ruddy, Conspicuous above a myriad!
texts.sng.5.11: His head [is] pure gold -- fine gold, His locks flowing, dark as a raven,
texts.sng.5.12: His eyes as doves by streams of water, Washing in milk, sitting in fulness.
texts.sng.5.13: His cheeks as a bed of the spice, towers of perfumes, His lips [are] lilies, dropping flowing myrrh,
texts.sng.5.14: His hands rings of gold, set with beryl, His heart bright ivory, covered with sapphires,
texts.sng.5.15: His limbs pillars of marble, Founded on sockets of fine gold, His appearance as Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
texts.sng.5.16: His mouth is sweetness -- and all of him desirable, This [is] my beloved, and this my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem!
texts.sng.6.1: Whither hath thy beloved gone, O fair among women? Whither hath thy beloved turned, And we seek him with thee?
texts.sng.6.2: My beloved went down to his garden, To the beds of the spice, To delight himself in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
texts.sng.6.3: I [am] my beloved's, and my beloved [is] mine, Who is delighting himself among the lilies.
texts.sng.6.4: Fair [art] thou, my friend, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Awe-inspiring as bannered hosts.
texts.sng.6.5: Turn round thine eyes from before me, Because they have made me proud. Thy hair [is] as a row of the goats, That have shone from Gilead,
texts.sng.6.6: Thy teeth as a row of the lambs, That have come up from the washing, Because all of them are forming twins, And a bereaved one is not among them.
texts.sng.6.7: As the work of the pomegranate [is] thy temple behind thy veil.
texts.sng.6.8: Sixty are queens, and eighty concubines, And virgins without number.
texts.sng.6.9: One is my dove, my perfect one, One she [is] of her mother, The choice one she [is] of her that bare her, Daughters saw, and pronounce her happy, Queens and concubines, and they praise her.
texts.sng.6.10: `Who [is] this that is looking forth as morning, Fair as the moon -- clear as the sun, Awe-inspiring as bannered hosts?'
texts.sng.6.11: Unto a garden of nuts I went down, To look on the buds of the valley, To see whither the vine had flourished, The pomegranates had blossomed --
texts.sng.6.12: I knew not my soul, It made me -- chariots of my people Nadib.
texts.sng.6.13: Return, return, O Shulammith! Return, return, and we look upon thee. What do ye see in Shulammith?
texts.sng.7.1: As the chorus of `Mahanaim.' How beautiful were thy feet with sandals, O daughter of Nadib. The turnings of thy sides [are] as ornaments, Work of the hands of an artificer.
texts.sng.7.2: Thy waist [is] a basin of roundness, It lacketh not the mixture, Thy body a heap of wheat, fenced with lilies,
texts.sng.7.3: Thy two breasts as two young ones, twins of a roe,
texts.sng.7.4: Thy neck as a tower of the ivory, Thine eyes pools in Heshbon, near the gate of Bath-Rabbim, Thy face as a tower of Lebanon looking to Damascus,
texts.sng.7.5: Thy head upon thee as Carmel, And the locks of thy head as purple, The king is bound with the flowings!
texts.sng.7.6: How fair and how pleasant hast thou been, O love, in delights.
texts.sng.7.7: This thy stature hath been like to a palm, And thy breasts to clusters.
texts.sng.7.8: I said, `Let me go up on the palm, Let me lay hold on its boughs, Yea, let thy breasts be, I pray thee, as clusters of the vine, And the fragrance of thy face as citrons,
texts.sng.7.9: And thy palate as the good wine --' Flowing to my beloved in uprightness, Strengthening the lips of the aged!
texts.sng.7.10: I [am] my beloved's, and on me [is] his desire.
texts.sng.7.11: Come, my beloved, we go forth to the field,
texts.sng.7.12: We lodge in the villages, we go early to the vineyards, We see if the vine hath flourished, The sweet smelling-flower hath opened. The pomegranates have blossomed, There do I give to thee my loves;
texts.sng.7.13: The mandrakes have given fragrance, And at our openings all pleasant things, New, yea, old, my beloved, I laid up for thee!
texts.sng.8.1: Who doth make thee as a brother to me, Sucking the breasts of my mother? I find thee without, I kiss thee, Yea, they do not despise me,
texts.sng.8.2: I lead thee, I bring thee in unto my mother's house, She doth teach me, I cause thee to drink of the perfumed wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate,
texts.sng.8.3: His left hand [is] under my head, And his right doth embrace me.
texts.sng.8.4: I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, How ye stir up, And how ye wake the love till she please!
texts.sng.8.5: Who [is] this coming from the wilderness, Hasting herself for her beloved? Under the citron-tree I have waked thee, There did thy mother pledge thee, There she gave a pledge [that] bare thee.
texts.sng.8.6: Set me as a seal on thy heart, as a seal on thine arm, For strong as death is love, Sharp as Sheol is jealousy, Its burnings [are] burnings of fire, a flame of Jah!
texts.sng.8.7: Many waters are not able to quench the love, And floods do not wash it away. If one give all the wealth of his house for love, Treading down -- they tread upon it.
texts.sng.8.8: We have a little sister, and breasts she hath not, What do we do for our sister, In the day that it is told of her?
texts.sng.8.9: If she is a wall, we build by her a palace of silver. And if she is a door, We fashion by her board-work of cedar.
texts.sng.8.10: I [am] a wall, and my breasts as towers, Then I have been in his eyes as one finding peace.
texts.sng.8.11: Solomon hath a vineyard in Baal-Hamon, He hath given the vineyard to keepers, Each bringeth for its fruit a thousand silverlings;
texts.sng.8.12: My vineyard -- my own -- is before me, The thousand [is] for thee, O Solomon. And the two hundred for those keeping its fruit. O dweller in gardens!
texts.sng.8.13: The companions are attending to thy voice, Cause me to hear. Flee, my beloved, and be like to a roe,
texts.sng.8.14: Or to a young one of the harts on mountains of spices!

texts.sng.1.2: ¡Oh si me besase de besos de su boca! porque mejores son tus amores que el vino.
texts.sng.1.3: Por el olor de tus buenos ungüentos, ungüento derramado es tu nombre: por tanto las doncellas te amaron.
texts.sng.1.4: Tírame en pos de ti, correremos. Metióme el rey en sus cámaras: gozarnos hemos, y alegrarnos hemos en ti: acordarnos hemos de tus amores, más que del vino. Los rectos te aman.
texts.sng.1.5: Morena soy, o! hijas de Jerusalem, mas de codiciar, como las cabañas de Cedar, como las tiendas de Salomón.
texts.sng.1.6: No miréis en que soy morena; porque el sol me miró: los hijos de mi madre se airaron contra mí: hiciéronme guarda de viñas, y mi viña, que era mía, no guardé.
texts.sng.1.7: Házme saber o! tú, a quien mi alma ama, donde repastas, donde haces tener majada al mediodía: Porque ¿por qué seré, como la que se aparta hacia los rebaños de tus compañeros?
texts.sng.1.8: Si tú no lo sabes, o! hermosa entre las mujeres, sálte por los rastros del rebaño, y apacienta tus cabritas junto a las cabañas de los pastores.
texts.sng.1.9: A una de las yeguas de los carros de Faraón te he comparado, o! amor mío.
texts.sng.1.10: Hermosas son tus mejillas entre los zarcillos, tu cuello entre los collares.
texts.sng.1.11: Zarcillos de oro te haremos, con clavos de plata.
texts.sng.1.12: Mientras que el rey estaba en su recostadero, mi espicanardi dio su olor.
texts.sng.1.13: Mi amado es para mi un manojico de mirra: que reposará entre mis pechos.
texts.sng.1.14: Racimo de cofer en las viñas de Engadí es para mí mi amado.
texts.sng.1.15: He aquí, que tú eres hermosa, o! compañera mía, he aquí, que tú eres hermosa: tus ojos de paloma.
texts.sng.1.16: He aquí, que tú eres hermoso, o! amado mío, también suave: también nuestro lecho florido.
texts.sng.1.17: Las vigas de nuestras casas son de cedro: las tablazones, de hayas.
texts.sng.2.1: Yo soy el lirio del campo, y la rosa de los valles.
texts.sng.2.2: Como el lirio entre las espinas, así es mi compañera entre las hijas.
texts.sng.2.3: Como el manzano entre los árboles monteses, así es mi amado entre los hijos: debajo de su sombra deseé sentarme, y me asenté, y su fruto ha sido dulce a mi paladar.
texts.sng.2.4: Trájome a la cámara del vino; y su bandera de amor puso sobre mí.
texts.sng.2.5: Sustentádme con frascos de vino, esforzádme con manzanas; porque estoy enferma de amor.
texts.sng.2.6: Su izquierda esté debajo de mi cabeza, y su derecha me abrace.
texts.sng.2.7: Yo os conjuro, o! hijas de Jerusalem, por las gamas, o por las ciervas del campo, que no despertéis, ni hagáis velar al amor, hasta que él quiera.
texts.sng.2.8: ¡La voz de mi amado! He aquí que éste viene saltando sobre los montes, saltando sobre los collados.
texts.sng.2.9: Mi amado es semejante al gamo, o al cabrito de los ciervos. Héle aquí, está detrás de nuestra pared, mirando por las ventanas, mostrándose por las rejas.
texts.sng.2.10: Mi amado habló, y me dijo: Levántate, o! amor mío, hermosa mía, y vente:
texts.sng.2.11: Porque, he aquí, ha pasado el invierno: la lluvia se ha mudado, y se fue;
texts.sng.2.12: Las flores se han mostrado en la tierra; el tiempo de la canción es venido, y voz de tórtola se ha oído en nuestra región;
texts.sng.2.13: La higuera ha metido sus higos, y las vides en cierne dieron olor: levántate, o! amor mío, hermosa mía, y vente.
texts.sng.2.14: Paloma mía, en los agujeros de la peña, en lo escondido de la escalera: muéstrame tu vista: házme oír tu voz; porque tu voz es dulce, y tu vista hermosa.
texts.sng.2.15: Tomádnos las zorras, las zorras pequeñas, que echan a perder las viñas, mientras nuestras viñas están en cierne.
texts.sng.2.16: Mi amado es mío, y yo suya: él apacienta entre lirios.
texts.sng.2.17: Hasta que apunte el día, y las sombras huyan, tórnate, o! amado mío: sé semejante al gamo, o al cabrito de los ciervos sobre los montes de Beter.
texts.sng.3.1: Por las noches busqué en mi cama al que ama mi alma; le busqué, y no le hallé.
texts.sng.3.2: Ahora pues levantarme he, y rodearé por la ciudad: por las calles, y por las plazas buscaré al que ama mi alma: le busqué, y no le hallé.
texts.sng.3.3: Halláronme las guardas que rondan por la ciudad, y les pregunté, diciendo: ¿Habéis visto al que ama mi alma?
texts.sng.3.4: Pasando de ellos un poco, luego hallé al que ama mi alma: trabé de él, y no le dejé, hasta que le metí en casa de mi madre, y a la cámara de la que me engendró.
texts.sng.3.5: Yo os conjuro, o! hijas de Jerusalem, por las gamas, o por las ciervas del campo, que no despertéis, ni hagáis velar a mi amor, hasta que él quiera.
texts.sng.3.6: ¿Quién es esta que sube del desierto como varas de humo, sahumada de mirra y de encienso, y de todos polvos aromáticos?
texts.sng.3.7: He aquí que la cama de Salomón sesenta fuertes la cercan, de los fuertes de Israel.
texts.sng.3.8: Todos ellos tienen espadas, diestros en la guerra: cada uno su espada sobre su muslo por los temores en las noches.
texts.sng.3.9: El rey Salomón se hizo un tálamo de madera del Líbano.
texts.sng.3.10: Sus columnas hizo de plata, su solado de oro, su cielo de grana, su interior solado de amor por las hijas de Jerusalem.
texts.sng.3.11: Salíd, o! hijas de Sión, y ved al rey Salomón con la corona con que le coronó su madre el día de su desposorio, y el día del gozo de su corazón.
texts.sng.4.1: He aquí que tú eres hermosa, o! amor mío, he aquí que tú eres hermosa: tus ojos, de paloma entre tus copetes; tu cabello, como manada de cabras que se muestran desde el monte de Galaad.
texts.sng.4.2: Tus dientes como manada de ovejas trasquiladas, que suben del lavadero: que todas ellas paren mellizos, y estéril no hay entre ellas.
texts.sng.4.3: Tus labios, como un hilo de grana, y tu habla hermosa: tus sienes, como pedazos de granada, dentro de tus copetes.
texts.sng.4.4: Tu cuello, como la torre de David edificada para enseñamientos: mil escudos están colgados de ella, todos escudos de valientes.
texts.sng.4.5: Tus dos pechos, como dos cabritos mellizos de gama, que son apacentados entre los lirios.
texts.sng.4.6: Hasta que apunte el día, y huyan las sombras, iré al monte de la mirra, y al collado del incienso.
texts.sng.4.7: Tú, toda eres hermosa, o! amor mío, y no hay mancha en ti.
texts.sng.4.8: Conmigo del Líbano, o! esposa mía, conmigo vendrás del Líbano: mirarás desde la cumbre de Amaná, desde la cumbre de Senir, y de Hermón: desde las moradas de los leones, desde los montes de los tigres.
texts.sng.4.9: Quitado me has mi corazón, hermana, esposa mía, quitado me has mi corazón, con uno de tus ojos, con un collar de tu cuello.
texts.sng.4.10: ¡Cuán hermosos son tus amores, o! hermana, esposa mía! ¡cuánto son mejores que el vino tus amores! ¡y el olor de tus ungüentos, que todas las especias aromáticas!
texts.sng.4.11: Panal de miel destilan tus labios, o! esposa mía: miel, y leche están debajo de tu lengua, y el olor de tus vestidos, como el olor del Líbano.
texts.sng.4.12: Huerto cerrado, o! hermana, esposa mía, fuente cerrada, fuente sellada.
texts.sng.4.13: Tus renuevos, como paraíso de granados con frutos suaves; alcanfores, y espicanardi.
texts.sng.4.14: Espicanardi y azafrán, caña aromática, y canela, con todos los árboles de incienso: mirra y áloes, con todas las principales especias.
texts.sng.4.15: Fuente de huertos, pozo de aguas vivas, que corren del Líbano.
texts.sng.4.16: Levántate aquilón, y ven, austro, sopla mi huerto, caigan sus especias. Venga mi amado a su huerto, y coma de su dulce fruta.
texts.sng.5.1: Yo vine a mi huerto, o! hermana, esposa mía; yo cogí mi mirra, y mis especias. Yo comí mi panal, y mi miel: yo bebí mi vino, y mi leche. Coméd amigos, bebéd amados, y embriagáos.
texts.sng.5.2: Yo duermo, y mi corazón vela. La voz de mi amado, que toca a la puerta, diciendo: Ábreme, hermana mía, amor mío, paloma mía, mi sin mancilla, porque mi cabeza está llena de rocío, mis guedejas de las gotas de la noche.
texts.sng.5.3: He desnudado mi ropa, ¿cómo la tengo de vestir? He lavado mis pies, ¿cómo los tengo de ensuciar?
texts.sng.5.4: Mi amado metió su mano por el agujero de la puerta, y mis entrañas rugieron dentro de mí.
texts.sng.5.5: Yo me levanté para abrir a mi amado, y mis manos gotearon mirra, y mis dedos mirra que pasaba sobre las aldabas del candado.
texts.sng.5.6: Yo abrí a mi amado: mas mi amado era ya ido, ya había pasado; y mi alma salió tras su hablar, le busqué, y no le hallé: le llamé, y no me respondió.
texts.sng.5.7: Halláronme las guardas, que rondan la ciudad: hiriéronme, llagáronme, quitáronme mi manto de encima, las guardas de los muros.
texts.sng.5.8: Yo os conjuro, o! hijas de Jerusalem, que si hallareis a mi amado, que le hagáis saber, que de amor estoy enferma.
texts.sng.5.9: ¿Qué es tu amado más que los otros amados, o! la más hermosa de todas las mujeres? ¿qué es tu amado más que los otros amados, que así nos has conjurado?
texts.sng.5.10: Mi amado es blanco, rubio, mas señalado que diez mil.
texts.sng.5.11: Su cabeza, oro fino; sus guedejas crespas, negras como el cuervo:
texts.sng.5.12: Sus ojos, como de las palomas, que están junto a los arroyos de las aguas, que se lavan con leche, que están junto a la abundancia.
texts.sng.5.13: Sus mejillas, como una era de especias aromáticas, como las flores de las especias: sus labios, lirios que gotean mirra que pasa.
texts.sng.5.14: Sus manos, anillos de oro engastados de jacintos: su vientre, blanco marfil cubierto de zafiros.
texts.sng.5.15: Sus piernas, columnas de mármol fundadas sobre basas de oro fino: su vista como el Líbano, escogido como los cedros.
texts.sng.5.16: Su paladar, dulzuras, y todo él deseos. Tal es mi amado, tal es mi amigo, o! hijas de Jerusalem.
texts.sng.6.1: ¿Dónde es ido tu amado, o! la más hermosa de todas las mujeres? ¿a dónde se apartó tu amado, y buscarle hemos contigo?
texts.sng.6.2: Mi amado descendió a su huerto a las eras de la especia, para apacentar en los huertos, y para coger los lirios.
texts.sng.6.3: Yo soy de mi amado, y mi amado es mío, el cual apacienta entre los lirios.
texts.sng.6.4: Hermosa eres tú, o! amor mío, como Tirsa: de desear, como Jerusalem: espantosa, como banderas de ejércitos.
texts.sng.6.5: Aparta tus ojos de delante de mí, porque ellos me vencieron. Tu cabello es como manada de cabras, que se muestran en Galaad.
texts.sng.6.6: Tus dientes, como manada de ovejas, que suben del lavadero: que todas paren mellizos, y estéril no hay entre ellas.
texts.sng.6.7: Como pedazos de granada son tus sienes entre tus copetes.
texts.sng.6.8: Sesenta son las reinas, y ochenta las concubinas; y las doncellas sin cuento.
texts.sng.6.9: Mas una es la paloma mía, la perfecta mía: única es a su madre, escogida a la que la engendró: viéronla las hijas, y llamáronla bienaventurada: las reinas y las concubinas la alabaron.
texts.sng.6.10: ¿Quién es esta que se muestra como el alba, hermosa como la luna, ilustre como el sol, espantosa como banderas de ejércitos?
texts.sng.6.11: A la huerta de los nogales descendí, para ver los frutos del valle, para ver si brotaban las vides, si florecían los granados.
texts.sng.6.12: No sé, mi alma me ha tornado como los carros de Aminadab.
texts.sng.6.13: Tórnate, tórnate, o! Sulamita: tórnate, tórnate, y mirarte hemos. ¿Qué veréis en la Sulamita? Como una compañía de reales.
texts.sng.7.1: ¡Cuán hermosos son tus pies en los calzados, o! hija del príncipe! Los cercos de tus muslos son como ajorcas, obra de mano de excelente maestro.
texts.sng.7.2: Tu ombligo, como una taza redonda, que no le falta bebida. Tu vientre, montón de trigo cercado de lirios.
texts.sng.7.3: Tus dos pechos, como dos cabritos mellizos de gama.
texts.sng.7.4: Tu cuello, como torre de marfil: tus ojos como las pesqueras de Jesebón junto a la puerta de Bat-rabem: tu nariz, como la torre del Líbano, que mira hacia Damasco.
texts.sng.7.5: Tu cabeza encima de ti, como la grana; y el cabello de tu cabeza, como la púrpura del rey ligada en los corredores.
texts.sng.7.6: ¡Qué hermosa eres, y cuán suave, o! amor deleitoso!
texts.sng.7.7: Tu estatura es semejante a la palma; y tus pechos, a los racimos.
texts.sng.7.8: Yo dije: Yo subiré a la palma, asiré sus ramos; y tus pechos serán ahora como racimos de vid; y el olor de tus narices, como de manzanas.
texts.sng.7.9: Y tu paladar como el buen vino, que se entra a mi amado suavemente, y hace hablar los labios de los viejos.
texts.sng.7.10: Yo soy de mi amado, y conmigo es su deseo.
texts.sng.7.11: Ven, o! amado mío, salgamos al campo, moremos en las aldeas.
texts.sng.7.12: Levantémosnos de mañana a las viñas: veamos si brotan las vides, si se abre el cierne, si han florecido los granados: allí te daré mis amores.
texts.sng.7.13: Las mandrágoras han dado olor; y en nuestras puertas hay todas dulzuras, nuevas, y viejas. Amado mío, yo las he guardado para ti.
texts.sng.8.1: ¡Oh quién te me diese, como hermano, que mamaste los pechos de mi madre! ¡Qué te hallase yo fuera, y te besase, y que no te menospreciasen!
texts.sng.8.2: ¡Qué yo te llevase, que yo te metiese en casa de mi madre: que me enseñases, que te hiciese beber vino adobado, del mosto de mis granadas!
texts.sng.8.3: Su izquierda esté debajo de mi cabeza, y su derecha me abrace.
texts.sng.8.4: Yo os conjuro, o! hijas de Jerusalem, ¿por qué despertaréis, y por qué haréis velar al amor, hasta que él quiera?
texts.sng.8.5: ¿Quién es esta, que sube del desierto recostada sobre su amado? Debajo de un manzano te desperté: allí tuvo dolores de ti tu madre; allí tuvo dolores la que te parió.
texts.sng.8.6: Pónme, como un sello, sobre tu corazón, como un signo sobre tu brazo; porque fuerte es como la muerte el amor: duro como el sepulcro el celo: sus brasas, brasas de fuego, llama fuerte.
texts.sng.8.7: Las muchas aguas no podrán apagar al amor: ni los ríos le cubrirán. Si diese hombre toda la hacienda de su casa por este amor, menospreciando la menospreciarán.
texts.sng.8.8: Tenemos una pequeña hermana, que no tiene aun pechos: ¿qué haremos a nuestra hermana, cuando de ella se hablare?
texts.sng.8.9: Si ella es muro, edificaremos sobre él un palacio de plata. Y si fuere puerta, guarnecerla hemos con tablas de cedro.
texts.sng.8.10: Yo soy muro, y mis pechos son como torres desde que yo fui en sus ojos como la que halla paz.
texts.sng.8.11: Salomón tuvo una viña en Baal-hamón, la cual entregó a guardas: cada uno de los cuales traerá mil piezas de plata por su fruto.
texts.sng.8.12: Mi viña, que es mía delante de mí: las mil piezas serán tuyas, o! Salomón; y doscientas, de los que guardan su fruto.
texts.sng.8.13: ¡Ah la que estás en los huertos! los compañeros escuchan tu voz: házme oír.
texts.sng.8.14: Huye, o! amado mío, y sé semejante al gamo, o al cervatillo de los ciervos, a las montañas de las especias.

texts.sng.1.1: The Song of Songs, which pertaineth to Solomon.
texts.sng.1.2: [SHE] Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! [THEY] For better are thy caresses than wine:
texts.sng.1.3: Like the fragrance of thy precious oils, Oil poured out, is thy name, For this cause, virgins love thee.
texts.sng.1.4: [SHE] Draw me! [THEY] After thee, will we run! [SHE] The king, hath brought me, into his chambers. [THEY] We will exult and rejoice in thee, we will mention thy caresses, beyond wine, Sincerely they love thee.
texts.sng.1.5: [SHE] Swarthy, I am but comely, ye daughters of Jerusalem. [THEY] Like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
texts.sng.1.6: [SHE] Do not look on me, because, I, am so swarthy, because the sun hath scorched me,—My mother’s sons, were angry with me, they set me to keep the vineyards, Mine own vineyard, have I not kept. …
texts.sng.1.7: Tell me, thou loved of my soul! Where wilt thou pasture thy flock? Where wilt thou let them recline at noon? For why should I be as one that wrappeth a veil about her, by the flocks of thy companions?
texts.sng.1.8: [HE] If thou know not of thyself, most beautiful among women! get thee forth in the footsteps of the flock, and pasture thy kids by the huts of the shepherds. …
texts.sng.1.9: To a mare of mine, in the chariots of Pharaoh, have I likened thee, my fair one!
texts.sng.1.10: Comely are thy cheeks, with bead-rows, thy neck, with strings of gems.
texts.sng.1.11: [THEY] Rows of golden ornaments, will we make thee, with studs of silver.
texts.sng.1.12: [SHE] By the time the king is in his circle, my nard, will have given out its fragrance:
texts.sng.1.13: A bag of myrrh, is my beloved to me, between my breasts, shall it tarry the night!
texts.sng.1.14: A cluster of henna, is my beloved to me, in the vineyards of En-gedi.
texts.sng.1.15: [HE] Lo! thou art beautiful my fair one, lo! thou art beautiful, Thine eyes, [are] doves!
texts.sng.1.16: [SHE] Lo! thou art beautiful, my beloved, Yea delightful! [BOTH] Yea! our couch, is covered with leaves:
texts.sng.1.17: The beams of our house, are cedars, Our fretted ceiling, is cypress-trees.
texts.sng.2.1: [SHE] I am The meadow-saffron of Sharon, The lily of the valleys.
texts.sng.2.2: [HE] As a lily among thorns, So, is my fair one, among the daughters!
texts.sng.2.3: [SHE] As an apple-tree among the trees of the forest, So, is my beloved, among the sons: In his shade, I greatly delighted and sat down, And, his fruit, was sweet to my taste.
texts.sng.2.4: He hath brought me into the house of wine, and, his banner over me, is love.
texts.sng.2.5: Sustain me with raisin-cakes, refresh me with apples,—for sick with love, I am.
texts.sng.2.6: His left hand under my head, then, his right hand, embraceth me!
texts.sng.2.7: [HE] I adjure you, ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the hinds of the field,—That ye wake not, nor arouse, the dear love until she please! [****]
texts.sng.2.8: [SHE] The voice of my beloved! Lo! here he cometh,—leaping over the mountains, skipping over the hills.
texts.sng.2.9: Resembleth, my beloved, a gazelle, or a young stag,—Lo! here he is, standing behind our wall, looking in at the windows, peeping in at the lattice.
texts.sng.2.10: Responded my beloved, and said to me,—Rise up! my fair—my beautiful—one, and come away,
texts.sng.2.11: For lo, the winter, is past,—the rain, is over, [and] gone;
texts.sng.2.12: The flowers, have appeared in the earth, the time of the spring-song, hath come,—and, the voice of the turtle, is heard in our land;
texts.sng.2.13: The fig-tree, hath spiced her green figs, and, the vines—all blossom, yield fragrance,—Rise up! my fair—my beautiful—one, and come away!
texts.sng.2.14: [HE] O my dove! In the retreats of the crag, in the hiding-place of the terrace, Let me see thy form, Let me hear thy voice,—For, thy voice, is sweet, and, thy form, comely.
texts.sng.2.15: [BOTH] Take ye for us, the foxes, the little foxes that are spoiling the vines,—and, our vines, are all blossom!
texts.sng.2.16: [SHE] My beloved, is, mine, and, I, am, his, he that pastureth among lilies!
texts.sng.2.17: Until the day, breathe, and the shadows, be lengthened, Again, liken thyself, my beloved, to a gazelle, or to a young stag, upon the cleft mountains. [****]
texts.sng.3.1: [SHE] Upon my couch, in the night-time, sought I the beloved of my soul,—I sought him, but found him not.
texts.sng.3.2: Come! I must arise, and go about in the city, In the paths and in the broadways, I must seek the beloved of my soul,—I sought him, but found him not.
texts.sng.3.3: The watchmen that go round in the city, found me, The beloved of my soul, have ye seen?
texts.sng.3.4: Scarcely had I passed from them, when I found the beloved of my soul,—I caught him, and would not let him go, until that I had brought him into the house of my mother, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
texts.sng.3.5: [HE] I adjure you ye, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles, or by the hinds of the field,—That ye wake not, nor arouse, the dear love until she please. [****]
texts.sng.3.6: [THEY] Who is this, coming up out of the wilderness, like pillars of smoke,—with perfume of myrrh, and frankincense, besides all the aromatic powder of the merchant?
texts.sng.3.7: Lo! his couch,’tis Solomon’s own, Threescore heroes, around it,—of the heroes of Israel:
texts.sng.3.8: All of them, grasping the sword, trained for war,—every man, with his sword upon his thigh, because of dread, in the night-time.
texts.sng.3.9: A palanquin, King Solomon made himself, of the trees of Lebanon:
texts.sng.3.10: The supports thereof, made he of silver, the couch thereof, of gold, the seat thereof, of purple,—the midst thereof, hath an inlay of love from the daughters of Jerusalem.
texts.sng.3.11: Go forth and gaze, ye daughters of Zion, upon King Solomon,—wearing the crown, wherewith his mother, crowned him, in the day of his marriage, and in the day of his heart gladness.
texts.sng.4.1: [HE] Lo! thou art beautiful, my fair one, Lo! thou art beautiful, Thine eyes, are doves, from behind thy veil,—Thy hair, is like a flock of goats, which are reclining on the sides of Mount Gilead:
texts.sng.4.2: Thy teeth, are like a flock, evenly grown, which have come up from the washing-place,—whereof, all of them, are twin-bearers, and bereaved, is none among them:
texts.sng.4.3: Like a cord of crimson, are thy lips, and, thy mouth, is lovely,—Like a slice of pomegranate, are thy temples, behind thy veil:
texts.sng.4.4: Like the tower of David, is thy neck, built for war,—A thousand shields, hung thereon, all, equipment of heroes:
texts.sng.4.5: Thy two breasts, are like two young roes, twins of a gazelle,—which pasture among lilies.
texts.sng.4.6: Until the day, breathe, and the shadows, be lengthened, I will get me unto the mountain of myrrh, and unto the hill of frankincense.
texts.sng.4.7: Thou art, all over, beautiful, my fair one, and, blemish, is there none in thee.
texts.sng.4.8: With me, from Lebanon, O bride, with me, from Lebanon, shalt thou enter,—Thou shalt look round from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir, and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
texts.sng.4.9: Thou hast encouraged me, my sister, bride,—thou hast encouraged me, with one [glance] of thine eyes, with one ornament of thy neck.
texts.sng.4.10: How beautiful are thy caresses, my sister, bride,—how much more delightful thy caresses, than wine, and the fragrance of thine oils, than all spices:
texts.sng.4.11: With sweetness, thy lips do drip, O bride,—Honey and milk, are under thy tongue, and, the fragrance of thy garments, is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
